# Acts of Thomas — Chapter 13
**Agent:** PNEUMA (Dynamic)
**Source:** Syriac MS / Greek recension, Acts of Thomas 13

---

*[THE MARTYRDOM OF THOMAS.]*

1. The king sat down with Charisius and Misdaeus and they made their decision: Thomas had to die. But they were afraid — too many people loved him to do it openly.

2. So they took him out of the city in the dark, with four soldiers and Charisius in charge, and they marched him up to a hill outside the walls. That is where they killed him.

3. But first — before they took him — Thomas gathered his people around him one last time. He looked at them and he spoke:

4. "Believe in the Lord Jesus Christ whom I have preached to you. Love each other the way he loved you. Don't let the troubles of this world fool you — because the troubles of this world are nothing, nothing at all, compared to the rest that is waiting for you.

5. Remember the poor. Take care of them. That is Christ's own work. Don't be afraid of suffering — the suffering of this short time cannot even be measured against the glory that is coming.

6. And above everything else — guard the seal you have received. Keep holy what is holy. Without it, there is no entering the kingdom."

7. Then he went with them. Willingly.

8. At the mountain he said to the soldiers: "The will of my Lord be done."

9. Then he prayed — quietly, simply: "My Lord and my God. You know everything. You know what I have suffered. You know the work I have done. You know I tried to do your will every day of my life. Now receive me."

10. He looked at Charisius and the soldiers. "Don't hate me as you do this," he said. "I am choosing this."

11. And the four soldiers drove their spears into him. He fell.

12. The believers who were there broke into weeping and lamentation.

13. Mygdonia was there. Tertia was there. Both of them weeping.

14. Thomas was dead.

15. They wrapped his body in fine linen and placed him in an old tomb — the kind that had once held the ancient kings.

16. Siphor and Gad would not leave. They stayed beside the body until he was buried.

---
*PNEUMA note: The martyrdom of Thomas is one of the most restrained death scenes in the apocryphal acts. There are no miracles at his death, no supernatural light, no vindication — only spears and falling and grief. His prayer ("receive me") is three words in the Syriac. His request to the soldiers ("don't hate me as you do this; I am choosing this") is the willingness of the Lamb. Mygdonia and Tertia are named last among the living — the women who have paid the greatest earthly price for faith stand at the foot of the martyrdom.*
